text:
A: Hello there. Can you hear me all right?
B: Hi, yeah, I can hear you. I'm Kerry.
A: Gareth. Nice to meet you. Is that the dog I saw in your photo, in the bed by the doors?
B: Yeah, that's Biscuit. He's asleep now, which is a miracle.
A: Lovely. What is he, a cockapoo?
B: Yeah, a cockapoo. He's four. Lovely nature, but he chews the skirting boards. Mark's given up painting them.
A: [laughs] We had a collie that ate a door frame once. The old lad's been gone two years now, and I'm trying to talk Helen, my wife, into another. I think I need ammunition, to be honest. Are they easy, cockapoos? Do they shed?
B: Not really, no, that's the main thing. No hair on the sofa. They need a lot of walking, though. We go up Cleeve Hill at weekends with him.
A: Not much hair on the sofa. Right, that's going straight to Helen. That's her big objection, the settee. Cleeve Hill, is that the one with the common on top?
B: Yeah, the common. The views are nice. I'm not a big walker, it's mainly for the dog, you know.
A: That's how it starts. Get a dog, and suddenly you're up a hill in the rain every Sunday. That's half my job, really. I'm a countryside ranger, up in Darwen.
B: Oh, right. So you're outdoors all day?
A: Most of it. Paths, woods, a reservoir, school groups. Bit of paperwork that I put off till the last minute. What do you do yourself?
B: I'm a senior service advisor at a car dealership, near Cheltenham. So I book the cars in, explain what needs doing, sell service plans, that sort of thing.
A: Oh, you'd have a field day with my van. It's a council one, it's about twelve years old, it makes a noise like a bag of spanners going up the hill.
B: [laughs] Yeah, I'd be booking that straight in. And probably selling you a service plan.
A: Go on, then. Do people kick off much? I'd have thought cars get people wound up.
B: They do, yeah. Someone this morning shouted at me because his car wasn't ready, but he'd brought it in two hours late. You just stay calm and let them get it out, and then they usually calm down.
A: Let them get it out. That's exactly it. Same with my volunteers, believe it or not. And the odd dog walker who's had a run-in with a cyclist.
B: Yeah, it's the same, isn't it. People just want to be listened to.
A: They do. Have you got kids an' all, or just the dog?
B: Two. Isla's eleven and Jacob's eight. So it's the school run, after-school clubs, and work never lines up. I'm shattered most days, honestly.
A: I remember that. Ours are twenty-four and twenty-one now, both moved out. You'll miss the chaos, I promise you. The house goes dead quiet.
B: I can't imagine it being quiet. Sounds quite nice right now, though. [laughs]
A: [laughs] Fair enough. Do you get away much, the four of you?
B: Once a year, usually. Lanzarote next summer, probably, all-inclusive. I'm trying to book early for the deal. Mark wants a hot tub for the garden as well, so we'll see what we can afford.
A: Hot tub. Now, Helen would like that more than a dog, I reckon. I might be shooting myself in the foot telling her about this call.
B: [laughs] Tell her the dog first, then.
A: Dog first, hot tub later. That's sound advice, that. Do you know what, I think
